input.quote: 28.1 This Agreement and each dispute arising from it are governed by the laws of the State of New York, without regard to conflict-of-law principles. ... 28.2 The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York have exclusive jurisdiction, and each Party irrevocably submits to personal jurisdiction and waives any objection based on venue or inconvenient forum. Nothing prevents a Party from seeking temporary injunctive relief in another court with jurisdiction to protect confidential information or intellectual property.
input.rationale: Section 28 sits at our preferred position: § 28.1 selects New York law (and disapplies the CISG), and § 28.2 confers exclusive jurisdiction on the state and federal courts in New York County with irrevocable submission and a venue/forum-non-conveniens waiver. The carve-out permitting temporary injunctive relief in another court is a customary interim-relief exception and does not defeat the exclusive merits forum. There is no arbitration provision anywhere in the Agreement (§ 28.3 is only a pre-filing executive escalation that expressly does not delay urgent relief or limitations-preserving filings), and § 30 contains no competing dispute forum. No redline required.
